$comment: Retail health plans with a maternity benefit, as quoted on an aggregator on 17 Oct 2026 for a couple in Bengaluru. Kavach shows these only as illustrative options at a hand-off (P5: category-level advice, no selling). Every plan here has a maternity waiting period, so it must be bought at least a year before the delivery to help. Premiums are not stored: they change with age, city and sum insured. The Star brochure is not stored here (it is Star Health's copyrighted document; download the current one from starhealth.in, Star Women Care); the IndusInd facts come from the aggregator's summary and still need the policy wording.
source: Aggregator comparison shared by the household (links expire; facts copied here)

options.insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Co. Ltd.
notes: Delivery expenses are a sub-limit per policy year that scales with the sum insured; ₹50,000 is the figure quoted for the sum insured chosen.

The brochure lists a 24-month delivery waiting period for the ₹5 lakh and ₹10 lakh sums insured and 12 months from ₹15 lakh; the aggregator quote said 12 months. Verify against the policy wording before relying on it.
Brochure: the current Star Women Care brochure on starhealth.in (not stored in this repo)
Maternity ₹2,00,000 for the mother after a 12-month wait; a further ₹1,00,000 for the newborn, covered from day 1 to day 90 at no extra premium.
Only the aggregator's summary is available; the UIN and wording are still to be collected.

lesson.fromClaim: A real 2025 Bengaluru normal delivery billed about ₹76,000; the employer group policy paid its ₹50,000 maternity cap and the family paid the rest, although the room was within the limit.
lesson.advice: At the 'baby on the way' moment Kavach should say: the company policy caps maternity; a retail plan with maternity only helps if bought 12 months or more before the delivery; add the newborn to the policy within 90 days.
